items.title: No account of how families understand the end of fluoridation
items.whyItMatters: The council's next consultation will rest on assumptions.
items.opportunity: Interview parents directly, sampled by neighbourhood deprivation and children's decay risk.

items.title: The most affected families are the least heard
items.whyItMatters: Consultations are dominated by organised groups (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Recruit through children's centres, school nurses and community groups, with interpreters.

items.title: Dental teams' role is undefined
items.whyItMatters: Dentists feel left to explain the decision.
items.opportunity: Include dental teams and school nurses as a separate group.

items.title: Local decay data cannot carry a causal claim
items.whyItMatters: Small numbers and a provider change.
items.opportunity: Use the data only as context in the interview guide, not as a finding.

items.title: Polarisation may silence participants
items.whyItMatters: People may hide views in mixed groups.
items.opportunity: Separate focus groups by role and view; offer one-to-one interviews.

reevaluation: The gaps confirm a qualitative study with purposive sampling of families most affected.
summary: Five gaps; the missing family perspective and the unheard families are high severity.
